summary: DevOps is the loop's long-lived-process substrate: ProcessManager starts, health-checks, tails, restarts, and shuts down background processes (dev servers, watchers, DBs) so they persist across agent steps. It turns ephemeral shell calls into ManagedProcess objects with health-check regex patterns, bounded log buffers, port reservation, and auto-restart with backoff, giving the loop stable services to act against without re-spawning them each iteration.
context_basis: recommendations were formed with src/devops/process_manager.rs read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), where managed processes must survive many loop iterations and feed bounded log tails back into the agent's context.

examples.title: Start a dev server as a ManagedProcess
examples.intent: Launch `npm run dev` once and keep it alive across all subsequent loop steps.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ProcessManager.start spawns the child under a ProcessConfig and tracks it as a ManagedProcess, so later iterations act against a running server instead of re-spawning it.

inputs_from: reason-stage decision to run a service

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging a command chip onto the process lane spawns a new process node bound to that command.
touch_interaction.visual: The node appears in Starting yellow, then transitions to Running green once spawned.

examples.mini_scenario: The agent drags 'npm run dev' into the process lane; a ManagedProcess starts and stays alive for the rest of the loop.
examples.pitfall: A ProcessConfig id must be unique; reusing an id for a second start collides with the existing ManagedProcess entry.

examples.title: Gate readiness on a health-check regex
examples.intent: Only proceed once the process prints its ready marker.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The health_check_pattern (e.g. 'Compiled successfully|Ready on http') sets health_matched, so the loop blocks on readiness before the act stage hits the service.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the process node opens its health-pattern editor.
touch_interaction.visual: A progress ring spins until the regex matches, then snaps to a solid green 'ready' badge.

examples.mini_scenario: The loop waits until 'Ready on http://localhost:3000' matches, then runs the browser test step.
examples.pitfall: Health check has a timeout (default 60s); a too-strict pattern that never matches leaves the process HealthCheckFailed.

examples.title: Tail the last N log lines into agent context
examples.intent: Give the LLM the most recent process output without unbounded context growth.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The log_buffer keeps up to MAX_LOG_LINES (500) LogLines; recent_logs feeds a bounded tail into the perceive stage each iteration.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking up on the process node scrolls its live log tail.
touch_interaction.visual: Stderr lines tint red, stdout lines grey; the buffer caps and older lines fade off the top.

examples.mini_scenario: After an edit, the agent reads the last 40 tailed lines and sees a fresh compile error to fix.
examples.pitfall: Each line is capped at MAX_LOG_LINE_LEN (10KB); a single huge line is truncated, so don't rely on full payloads in logs.

examples.title: Auto-restart a crashed process with backoff
examples.intent: Keep a flaky service available without manual intervention.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: When auto_restart is set, a Crashed status transitions to Restarting{attempt} up to max_restart_attempts, so the loop keeps acting against a service that recovers itself.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the process node reveals restart policy and current attempt count.
touch_interaction.visual: On crash the node flashes red then pulses amber 'Restarting (2/5)' while backing off.

examples.mini_scenario: The dev server crashes on a bad import; it auto-restarts on attempt 2 after the agent fixes the file.
examples.pitfall: max_restart_attempts of 0 means unlimited; a persistently broken service can restart-loop forever and burn resources.

examples.title: Reserve a port before binding
examples.intent: Avoid port conflicts when spinning up multiple services.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A PortReservation holds a TcpListener with a TTL (PORT_RESERVATION_TTL, 30s), so the control stage can claim a port before the process actually binds it.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the port pin on a process node reserves that port and shows the countdown.
touch_interaction.visual: A small port chip glows blue with a shrinking TTL ring; conflicting ports flash red.

examples.mini_scenario: Before starting a second server, port 3001 is reserved so it won't collide with the running one on 3000.
examples.pitfall: Reservations expire after 30s; if the process doesn't bind in time the port is released and can be taken by another.

examples.title: Gracefully shut down and clean up
examples.intent: Terminate a process and release its resources at loop end.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ProcessManager.stop drives a ManagedProcess to Stopped with cleanup, so terminal loop states don't leak orphaned children or held ports.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking a process node off the lane sends a graceful stop.
touch_interaction.visual: The node dims to grey 'Stopped' and its port chip detaches and fades.

examples.mini_scenario: On loop completion the dev server is stopped cleanly and port 3000 is freed for the next run.
examples.pitfall: Skipping stop on Failed exits leaves orphaned children; always tear down in both Completed and Failed paths.

examples.title: Snapshot the process fleet as an inventory
examples.intent: Get one structured view of every managed process for the loop to reason over.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: try_inventory builds a ProcessInventory (totals by status + per-process summaries), giving the observe stage a single serializable picture of all background services.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the process lane collapses all nodes into one inventory summary card.
touch_interaction.visual: A card shows counts: running/starting/restarting/inactive, each with a colored tally.

examples.mini_scenario: The inventory reports 2 running, 1 restarting, and reserved ports [3000,3001] for the operator overlay.
examples.pitfall: try_inventory takes a log_lines arg per process; requesting large tails for many processes bloats the snapshot.

examples.title: Reconcile drifted process state
examples.intent: Detect processes that exited or leaked and clean the registry.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: reconcile scans handles and produces a ProcessReconcileReport (orphaned, exited, cleared, removed), keeping the loop's model of live services true to reality.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating the reconcile dial re-scans the fleet and updates each node's real status.
touch_interaction.visual: Nodes briefly desaturate during scan, then those found dead collapse with a puff animation.

examples.mini_scenario: Reconcile finds a server that exited silently, marks 1 exited and clears its handle so the loop stops treating it as live.
examples.pitfall: Reconcile mutates the registry; running it mid-start can race a process still transitioning through Starting.

examples.title: Restart on a health-marker regression
examples.intent: Recover when a running process stops meeting its health signal.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A process that flips to HealthCheckFailed can be driven back through Restarting, so control heals degraded services without operator input.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing an unhealthy node offers a 'restart' action.
touch_interaction.visual: The health badge flips from green to red; a restart triggers the amber Restarting pulse.

examples.mini_scenario: A watcher stops emitting 'Compiled successfully' after a broken change; the loop restarts it once fixed.
examples.pitfall: Restarting resets health_matched; downstream verify must re-wait for readiness rather than assume the old ready state.

examples.title: Pass environment into the ProcessConfig
examples.intent: Give a service the env vars it needs without polluting the global environment.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ProcessConfig.env carries a scoped HashMap into the spawned child, so foundation-level config flows to exactly the process that needs it.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the env slot opens a key/value sheet for that process.
touch_interaction.visual: Env keys render as small pills on the node's underside; secret values show masked.

examples.mini_scenario: The dev server node gets NODE_ENV=development and a masked API key injected via its ProcessConfig.env.
examples.pitfall: Env is per-process, not inherited-plus; forgetting to include PATH-critical vars can make the child fail to find its binary.

examples.title: Set the working directory for a service
examples.intent: Run a process in the correct project subdirectory.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ProcessConfig.cwd anchors the spawned process to a directory, so relative paths in the service resolve correctly across every loop iteration.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging a folder node onto a process node sets its cwd.
touch_interaction.visual: The process node shows a small folder tag with the directory basename.

examples.mini_scenario: The frontend server is pinned to cwd=./web so its relative config and asset paths resolve.
examples.pitfall: A missing/unreadable cwd makes spawn fail immediately; validate the path before wiring it into ProcessConfig.

examples.title: Distinguish stdout from stderr in the tail
examples.intent: Let the agent tell normal output from error output.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Each LogLine carries a LogStream (Stdout/Stderr) tag, so the perceive stage can weight stderr more heavily when deciding whether the service is failing.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the stderr filter toggle shows only error-stream lines.
touch_interaction.visual: Stderr lines carry a red left-bar; the toggle badge counts unread stderr lines.

examples.mini_scenario: A warning on stdout is ignored, but a stderr LogLine 'panic: index out of bounds' triggers a fix step.
examples.pitfall: Some tools log errors to stdout; don't assume stderr==error, cross-check with the log level in the content.

examples.title: Track uptime for a running service
examples.intent: Know how long a service has been stable.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ProcessSummary.uptime_secs derives from started_at, giving the observe stage a stability signal to gate long-running act steps.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the process node's clock badge shows uptime and restart count.
touch_interaction.visual: An uptime counter ticks upward; a recent restart resets it and briefly flashes.

examples.mini_scenario: The server shows 240s uptime with 0 restarts, so the loop trusts it for a heavy integration test.
examples.pitfall: Uptime resets on restart; a high restart_count with low uptime means unstable, not fresh-and-healthy.

examples.title: Detect a port conflict before start
examples.intent: Fail fast when the expected port is already taken.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: expected_port plus the reservation listener lets the verify stage detect a conflict up front instead of after a half-started process, avoiding a wasted iteration.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the port pin runs a bind test on that port.
touch_interaction.visual: A green check if free, a red X with 'in use' if the bind fails.

examples.mini_scenario: Before starting, port 3000 fails its bind test; the loop picks 3001 instead of crashing on start.
examples.pitfall: A free port at check time can be taken before spawn; treat the check as advisory, not a hard guarantee.

examples.title: Serialize a process for a session snapshot
examples.intent: Persist the fleet's shape across a session boundary.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ProcessSummary is Serialize/Deserialize, so the foundation layer can snapshot the fleet's config and status into a session and restore intent later.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the whole lane into a snapshot node freezes the fleet's serialized state.
touch_interaction.visual: The lane collapses into a single disk-icon card labeled with process count.

examples.mini_scenario: A session snapshot records the two servers' configs and ports so a resumed loop knows what should be running.
examples.pitfall: The live Child handle is not serializable; a restored snapshot describes intent but must re-spawn to get running processes.

examples.title: Run a one-shot build as a managed step
examples.intent: Run a finite build/test command and capture its full output.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A ProcessConfig with no health pattern runs to completion; its exit and log_buffer feed the verify stage a clean pass/fail with captured logs.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging a build chip in and out marks it as one-shot rather than persistent.
touch_interaction.visual: The node shows a single-run icon and self-collapses to Stopped when the build exits.

examples.mini_scenario: `cargo build` runs as a managed one-shot; on exit the loop reads the captured errors and the node collapses.
examples.pitfall: Don't set auto_restart on a one-shot; a completed build reported as Crashed would restart-loop endlessly.

examples.title: Backoff-limit restart storms
examples.intent: Stop a hopeless service from consuming the loop in restart churn.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: restart_count against max_restart_attempts bounds the Restarting cycle; once exceeded the process stays Crashed, letting control escalate instead of spinning.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the restart badge shows attempts used vs the cap.
touch_interaction.visual: The attempt counter fills a small bar; hitting the cap turns the node solid red 'Crashed'.

examples.mini_scenario: After 5 failed restarts the node stays Crashed and control routes the failure to the agent for diagnosis.
examples.pitfall: Escalate on cap-reached; silently leaving a Crashed process means the loop acts against a dead service.

examples.title: Feed compile errors from the tail into the fix loop
examples.intent: Close the loop from service output back to a code edit.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The bounded recent_logs of a watcher become reason-stage input, so the loop's next act (an edit) is chosen from the freshest error the process reported.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing an edge from the process log tail to the reason node routes errors into planning.
touch_interaction.visual: Red error lines flow along the edge into the reason node, which pulses as it ingests them.

examples.mini_scenario: The watcher tails 'expected `;`, found `}`'; the reason node plans an edit at that file and line.
examples.pitfall: Tails are bounded (500 lines); a burst that scrolls the real error off the top can mislead the fix decision.

examples.title: Keep a database connection alive across steps
examples.intent: Avoid reconnecting an expensive dependency every iteration.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A long-running DB process managed once stays Running across steps, so the foundation layer offers a stable connection rather than paying setup cost each loop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the DB node pins it as a shared dependency for all act nodes.
touch_interaction.visual: A persistent link icon connects the DB node to the loop spine; it glows steady green.

examples.mini_scenario: A local Postgres stays Running so each test step reuses it instead of spinning up a fresh container.
examples.pitfall: Persistent dependencies must still be stopped at teardown; a leaked DB process holds its port and data locks.

examples.title: Reconcile before restoring a session
examples.intent: Sync the registry with reality before trusting a restored fleet.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Running reconcile on resume produces a ProcessReconcileReport that prunes dead handles and reserved ports, so the resumed loop's verify stage starts from an accurate fleet.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating the reconcile dial on resume re-scans and rebuilds the lane from live processes.
touch_interaction.visual: Ghosted restored nodes solidify if alive or vanish if the reconcile finds them gone.

examples.mini_scenario: On resume, reconcile finds 1 of 2 restored servers actually dead, removes it, and frees its reserved port.
examples.pitfall: Trusting a raw restored snapshot skips reconcile; the loop then acts against processes that no longer exist.
